findings.issue: The register upsert does not check that the conflicting row belongs to the event's order. A CANCELLED part for order Y that names shipment X of order Z moves X to terminal CANCELLED. Since this change that is no longer just bookkeeping: recordDelivered then silently skips X's SALE, COMMISSION and FEE. The forged legacy path does the same: an orderId equal to a real shipment id builds Part(orderId=X) and cancels X. This needs Kafka write access or an order-service bug, and the existing trust model already accepts DELIVERED amounts from the same topic, so it is not a blocker.
findings.fix: Add `AND ledger_shipments.order_id = EXCLUDED.order_id` to the ON CONFLICT ... WHERE clause. In recordDelivered, select order_id together with status and apply the CANCELLED skip only when the order matches; otherwise log ids only, or dead-letter as reverse() does for a SALE from another order.

findings.issue: A wrongly or falsely suppressed SALE cannot be detected. A register row that is CANCELLED with no SALE is never compared with order-service, so a shipment that order-service reports as DELIVERED but a stray CANCELLED blocked is underpaid and nobody is alerted. The only trace is a WARN line.
findings.fix: Optional defence in depth that AC-8 still allows (AC-8 covers only rows that are CANCELLED in order-service too): for CANCELLED rows with no SALE that are past grace, ask order-service within the existing feign-error budget and report STATE_MISMATCH when it says DELIVERED. Alternatively, track it as a tech-debt item.

findings.issue: A legacy DELIVERED event (no shipments array) does not call track, so no register row exists when recordDelivered takes its FOR SHARE lock, and that lock covers no row. A legacy CANCELLED processed at the same time can commit its insert after the check, and the SALE is then booked after the cancel. Today this is unlikely because order.events is presumably keyed by orderId, so events for one order are processed one at a time.
findings.fix: Have the legacy DELIVERED branch call ledger.track with the DELIVERED part before recordDelivered, so the row exists and gets locked. Or document that this guarantee depends on orderId partition keying.

summary: No blocker or major on the seller money path. A replayed, out-of-order or inflated DELIVERED for a cancelled shipment books nothing; track commits first (REQUIRES_NEW) and recordDelivered reads the status under FOR SHARE, so a concurrent cancel either waits for the booking or is seen first, with no deadlock. CANCELLED-is-terminal stops replays and lower-rank events rewriting amount, seller or updated_at. A CANCELLED event cannot reverse booked entries (AC-4); it can only suppress a SALE that arrives after it. Minors: the upsert and booking guard do not check that the shipment belongs to the event's order (also the legacy orderId-as-shipmentId path); a CANCELLED row with no SALE is never checked against order-service; the legacy DELIVERED path has no register row to lock. Admin repair 409 rolls back, authz unchanged, constant message, ids-only WARN, bound SQL parameters, single-row short FOR SHARE lock, no new dependency.
